title: NASA’s Drone Traffic Management System Completes Final Tests
description: NASA's Unmanned Aircraft Systems Traffic Management project, or UTM, is working to safely integrate drones into low-altitude airspace. In 2019, the project completed its final phase of flight tests. The research results are being transferred to the Federal Aviation Administration, who will continue development of the UTM system and implement it over time.

transcript.text: NASA is getting the drone revolution off the ground.
Its Unmanned Aircraft Systems Traffic Management platform makes flying large numbers of drones at low altitude possible.
The technology lets drone operators define flight paths and share that information with others,
creating a system for operating drones safely and efficiently in populated and urban areas.
Several years of field testing concluded in 2019 with trials in Reno, Nevada, and Corpus Christi, Texas.
More than 35 industry and government partners participated in the flight tests.
These activities featured multiple vehicles flying beyond sight of their operators
in the airspace between the ground and 400 feet.
The tests also explored the ability of drones to operate under unexpected conditions.
Flight scenarios included loss of ground communications,
Onboard autonomous systems were also developed
to detect and avoid drones, determine safe landing locations, and improve vehicle-to-vehicle communications.
The Federal Aviation Administration will continue development of the system and implement it over time,
unleashing a world of new opportunities.
